topic: Robust ex-ante Zhao control-variate bases under cross-world dependence uncertainty. Freeze a finite known network and assignment law, two mutually exclusive exposure events, iid bounded potential-outcome pairs, and an independent unpaired pilot identifying F1,F0 but not their copula. K1 derive sharp Fréchet covariance endpoints by rearrangement and prove fixed-basis loss is affine, so the adversary is an endpoint. K2 maximize the smaller endpoint gain over normalized κ-regular block-separable projective bases, using certified interval branch-and-bound with ε-global guarantees and ε→0; claim neither an SDP reduction nor a universal minimax equality. K3 prove strictly lower worst-copula residual variance than Zhao's c=0 surrogate on a relative-open lawful neighborhood. K4 prove plug-in robust-value and outer argmax-set consistency, with point convergence only for an isolated unique saddle, then reanalyze Zhao's Jiangxi PICC network experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The triangle Bernoulli(1/3) witness gives the stated π and Ω; Bernoulli(1/2) margins admit observationally equivalent c=±1/4. Exact endpoint-mixture certificates give c=0 worst loss 521/1200 and robust constant loss 2613/8432, an absolute reduction 4912/39525 and a 28.62398% relative reduction. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the certified global solver and uniform relative-open dominance/argmax correspondence for the full κ-regular class. EARLY KILL TEST: Recheck the certificate equality sets and run interval branch-and-bound on the triangle; stop if any c=0 optimizer has worst loss ≤2613/8432 or the claimed outer set convergence fails.

open_problems.open_problem: For a fixed block-separable Zhao control-variate basis under two mutually exclusive network exposures, characterize the sharp Fréchet interval for the unidentified cross-world covariance and determine whether the basis loss is affine in that covariance, with the worst copula attained at an endpoint.

source_refs.claim: The optimal network-interference basis depends on an unidentified covariance between potential outcomes; the implementation sets it to zero and explicitly leaves robust bases under moment misspecification for future work.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: For two identified potential-outcome marginals, quantile rearrangements attain sharp covariance and randomization-variance endpoints and their empirical analogues consistently estimate those endpoints.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, Donald K. K. Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhao's paper identifies the covariance omission but does not reduce its structured network-basis criterion to a scalar dependence parameter. Aronow, Green, and Lee establish sharp rearrangement endpoints for difference-in-means variance under complete randomization, not for Zhao's block-separable projective loss. The missing step is an exact matrix expansion showing that every copula-dependent term collapses to one covariance with a basis-dependent affine coefficient; without that reduction, scalar Fréchet endpoints need not be sharp for the full network criterion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp partial-identification result giving the lower and upper quantile-coupling covariance endpoints, an explicit formula L_B(c)=α_B+β_Bc for every lawful fixed basis B, and an attainment proof that the supremum over compatible copulas equals max{L_B(c_L),L_B(c_U)}.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from rare network exposures to indicator control variates, optimal basis choice, and the unidentified covariance that forces the zero surrogate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rare network exposures inflate Horvitz-Thompson variance -> indicator control variates can cancel design randomness -> optimal bases require cross-potential-outcome moments -> an unidentified copula calls for sharp dependence-robust basis evaluation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the Hoeffding rearrangement inequality and comonotone/countermonotone quantile couplings to attain both covariance endpoints rather than merely bound them.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once Zhao's loss is shown affine in the one unidentified covariance, its ambiguity set is exactly the fixed-marginal coupling problem treated by the rearrangement proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply empirical-process convergence to adjusted-outcome empirical marginals and plug their quantile couplings into asymptotically sharp endpoint estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inference analogue in which variance-reducing adjustment changes the relevant marginals while the cross-world covariance remains unidentified.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the maximum smaller-endpoint gain over normalized κ-regular block-separable projective Zhao bases be computed by interval branch-and-bound with a finite ε-global certificate for every ε>0 and certified value and outer-solution-set convergence as ε tends to zero?

source_refs.claim: The network-interference basis problem is nonconvex; Zhao supplies a one-half approximation and an alternating local-search heuristic rather than a global optimizer.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: A branch-and-bound method for bounded nonconvex all-quadratic programs is proved to terminate within ε of the global minimum.
source_refs.author: Gary R. Reeves

source_refs.claim: The αBB method uses interval curvature bounds and convergent convex underestimators to provide global convergence guarantees for twice-differentiable constrained nonconvex programs.
source_refs.author: Claire S. Adjiman, Stefan Dallwig, Christodoulos A. Floudas, Arnold Neumaier

source_refs.excerpt: the certificate includes interval bounds for count truncation and the λ-tail
Its polynomial support reduction is existential rather than algorithmic.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature supplies generic ε-global branch-and-bound machinery, but Zhao's feasible set is projective, κ-regularity is needed to control inverse-matrix denominators, and the objective is the nonsmooth minimum of two endpoint gains. The closest prior CausalSmith certificate controls a one-dimensional Poisson tail, while another banked design result explicitly stops at an existential support reduction. The first new step is therefore an outward-rounded, inclusion-isotonic interval extension on compact quotient charts that remains valid at normalization boundaries and endpoint-tie surfaces; neither a generic SDP reduction nor Zhao's local heuristic establishes this.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A certified algorithm result specifying compact normalized κ-regular charts, boxwise upper and lower bounds for both endpoint gains and their minimum, safe pruning and subdivision, finite termination with value gap at most ε, and outer Painlevé-Kuratowski convergence of certified solution sets to the global argmax set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its computation section cleanly distinguishes a provable approximation from a local heuristic, providing the right setup for a global-certification contribution without implying an SDP reduction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal network control variates require a structured nonconvex basis problem -> a one-half approximation supplies a baseline -> alternating search gives only local improvement -> copula-robust maximin choice requires an auditable ε-global certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use interval Hessian bounds to construct convergent convex underestimators and prove that branch-and-bound closes the global optimality gap under subdivision.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On a κ-regular normalized chart the endpoint gains are smooth rational functions, so interval curvature bounds give a direct route to rigorous boxwise envelopes.

method_exemplars.technique: Maintain feasible incumbents and globally valid region bounds under bisection, with a finite ε-termination proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After normalization, the Zhao problem is a bounded nonconvex quadratic-rational program; Reeves provides the core certification logic that the rational and tie-surface extensions must preserve.

open_problems.open_problem: When pilot marginals F1 and F0 replace population marginals, do the Fréchet-robust Zhao value and full κ-regular projective-basis argmax correspondence converge, with only outer set convergence under ties and point convergence under an isolated unique normalized saddle?

source_refs.claim: Zhao uses sample splitting to estimate outcome moments and notes that basis quality depends on moment accuracy, but does not analyze a global copula-robust argmax correspondence.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: Empirical marginal distributions and quantiles consistently estimate scalar sharp Fréchet variance endpoints under bounded outcomes.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.claim: The fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in its marginals, so Berge's theorem yields continuous optimized values and upper-hemicontinuous optimizer sets.
source_refs.author: James Bergin

source_refs.excerpt: plug-in Chat_a_plus consistency needs uniform convergence / argmax-consistency

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar endpoint consistency does not control a nonconvex optimizer with projective duplicates, flat ridges, or a kink where the two endpoint gains tie. Bergin gives continuity of the coupling correspondence and Zhao discusses estimated moments, while the prior policy-value proposal records uniform feasible-class and argmax consistency as the undischarged proof bottleneck. The first new step is a uniform empirical-quantile bound for both endpoint objective surfaces over the entire κ-regular quotient, followed by a set-valued argmax theorem that does not silently assume uniqueness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform objective-convergence and stochastic epi-convergence result implying robust-value consistency and outer Painlevé-Kuratowski convergence of plug-in global argmax sets, plus point convergence under an explicit isolated-unique-saddle condition and a tie example where point convergence fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates data-driven basis choice and explains why inaccurate moments can degrade the selected basis; the independent unpaired pilot is the destination-specific repair.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal bases depend on unknown outcome laws -> an independent pilot identifies the two marginals but not their copula -> empirical Fréchet endpoints define a plug-in maximin problem -> ties and projective symmetries require set-valued consistency.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine uniform empirical-CDF convergence with quantile rearrangement formulas to control plug-in sharp endpoints under bounded outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unpaired pilot produces exactly the two empirical marginals used in their endpoint estimator; the new burden is uniformity over the Zhao basis class.

method_exemplars.technique: Use continuity of restricted-marginal measure correspondences with Berge's maximum theorem to obtain value continuity and upper hemicontinuity of optimizers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Outer convergence of robust basis sets is the finite-dimensional optimizer-correspondence analogue once endpoint surfaces converge uniformly.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive consistency and asymptotic distributions for plug-in bounds in a causal minimax problem with an unidentified potential-outcome copula.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how empirical Fréchet optimization can support inference, while Zhao's projective global argmax requires the additional set-valued step.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what explicit assignment-law, marginal-law, and saddle-separation conditions does a Fréchet-robust Zhao basis have strictly smaller worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer on a nonempty relative-open neighborhood of lawful instances?

source_refs.claim: The practical basis uses a zero cross-potential-outcome covariance surrogate, and robust basis choice under moment misspecification is explicitly left open.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: Distributionally robust optimization can model ambiguity in linear or rank dependence, including copulas, but does not address causal control-variate basis design.
source_refs.author: Rui Gao, Anton J. Kleywegt

source_refs.claim: Unidentified potential-outcome copulas are optimized over for treatment-effect prediction, but the target is a Wasserstein-shift prediction rule rather than a network control-variate basis.
source_refs.author: Ruonan Xu, Xiye Yang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Maximin optimization gives only weak improvement over the zero-covariance basis. Strict improvement can disappear when a zero-surrogate optimizer also optimizes both endpoints, an endpoint slope vanishes, the robust optimum is not isolated, or κ-regularity fails at the boundary. Existing copula-robust decision papers treat different losses, and Zhao gives no local separation theorem. Turning the proposed triangle calculation into a lawful neighborhood result requires a verified positive value gap and continuity of both endpoint losses and the feasible correspondence in the relative topology; it does not follow from a universal minimax equality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition result with checkable strict-separation and κ-regularity inequalities yielding δ>0 and a relative-open neighborhood U on which every robust optimum has worst-copula residual variance at least δ below every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer, together with boundary counterexamples showing why the conditions are needed.

writing_exemplar.why: The destination is Zhao's operational zero-covariance surrogate and its stated robustness limitation, with the Jiangxi network application making the performance consequence concrete.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cross-world covariance is unobserved -> implementation inserts zero -> a lawful alternative copula can make that basis fragile -> a separated robust saddle should deliver persistent worst-copula variance reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine continuity of the restricted-marginal coupling correspondence with Berge's maximum theorem to propagate a strict witness gap to nearby marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The neighborhood varies the same two marginals that generate the Fréchet class, so value and optimizer-correspondence continuity are exactly what makes strict dominance persist.

method_exemplars.technique: Place dependence ambiguity directly in the decision problem and compare the worst-case value of a robust action with a nominal-dependence action.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the decision-theoretic template for replacing a nominal correlation by a dependence-robust optimizer; Zhao supplies the experiment-specific loss and feasible basis geometry.

open_problems.open_problem: Given only unpaired pilot marginals F1 and F0, characterize the sharp jointly attainable vector of all basis-induced cross-world covariance terms under one common copula and determine when the Cartesian product of coordinatewise Fréchet intervals is exact.

source_refs.excerpt: pointwise Makarov sharpness is not enough for finite vectors or functionals of the DTE CDF

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar covariance endpoints follow from rearrangement, but independently stacking endpoints across basis blocks can use a different extremizing copula in each coordinate. The archived DTE proposal records the analogous failure of pointwise Makarov sharpness for finite vectors and functionals. The first changed proof step is to replace scalar rearrangement by the support function of a vector-valued covariance kernel over one Kantorovich coupling; without this common-copula geometry, a blockwise robust objective can optimize over an unlawfully rectangular ambiguity set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A support-function or optimal-transport dual characterization of the joint covariance region, a necessary-and-sufficient condition for rectangularity, and a finite lawful witness proving strict containment when coordinatewise endpoint copulas are incompatible.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves from attractive pointwise marginal bounds to the harder simultaneous-sharpness question for vectors or functionals, which is the exact warning needed here.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Marginals identify scalar Fréchet envelopes -> a block basis combines several cross-world covariance functionals -> coordinatewise sharpness may not paste to one joint law -> the robust design needs a common-copula covariance region.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive sharp extremal-coupling bounds from fixed potential-outcome marginals using Fréchet-Makarov constructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its scalar coupling construction is the starting point that must be lifted to a vector of basis-induced covariance functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent fixed-marginal joint-potential-outcome bounds as an optimal-transport primal and dual over couplings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested covariance region is a vector-valued optimal-transport image, and each support-function direction reduces to a scalar transport problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct confidence regions for interval-identified parameters while accounting for estimated endpoints and nonzero identified-set width.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the joint support function is estimated from pilot marginals, inference must retain its nonsmooth endpoint and tie geometry rather than treat the covariance vector as point identified.

literature_map:
Zhao (2026, arXiv:2608.15333) is the direct anchor: optimal network-interference control-variate bases solve a nonconvex problem, while implementation sets unidentified cross-world covariance to zero and explicitly leaves robust basis choice open.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1405.6555) give sharp Fréchet covariance/variance endpoints and empirical-quantile estimators under complete randomization.
Mikhaeil and Green (2024, arXiv:2411.00191) extend sharp covariance-based variance bounds to general regression adjustment, but not network exposure designs or ex-ante basis optimization.
Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje (2026, JASA; arXiv:2112.01709) optimize conservative quadratic variance bounds under arbitrary interference and designs, addressing variance estimation rather than copula-robust basis choice.
Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics; arXiv:1305.6156) supply the known-exposure-mapping and IPW design-based foundation under general interference.
Leung (2022, Econometrica; arXiv:1911.07085) supplies approximate-neighborhood-interference asymptotics and network-HAC bias analysis.
Gao and Ding (2025, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2309.07476) give regression/Hájek design-based analysis and an adjusted network-robust covariance estimator.
Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet (2015, AEJ Applied) are the Jiangxi PICC application anchor reused by Zhao for the directed friendship network and exposure contrasts.
Gao and Kleywegt (2017, arXiv:1701.04200) develop dependence- and copula-aware distributionally robust optimization for noncausal decision losses.
Xu and Yang (2025, arXiv:2512.12781) optimize over unidentified potential-outcome copulas for treatment-effect prediction and derive plug-in inference, a close but distinct target.
Bergin (1999, Economic Theory) proves continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, providing the maximum-theorem route to robust values and outer optimizer stability.
Reeves (1975, Management Science) proves finite ε-global branch-and-bound for bounded nonconvex all-quadratic programs.
Adjiman, Dallwig, Floudas, and Neumaier (1998, Computers & Chemical Engineering) provide interval-curvature and convex-underestimator machinery for rigorous global optimization.
The live tension is precise: rearrangement theory collapses copula ambiguity to endpoints only after Zhao's network-basis loss is proved affine in the relevant common-copula functional, and no located paper globally certifies the resulting κ-regular projective maximin problem.
